_comment: ICSF callable services as COBOL calls them: each service's parameters in CALL ... USING order, its keywords in this project's words, and the IBM topic each was read from on the retrieved date. lib/sets/crypto.mjs reads the findings section, whose keywords are the ones each rule reports, with the reason each is weak.

document.title: z/OS Cryptographic Services ICSF Application Programmer's Guide
document.edition: June 2025, z/OS 3.1 (Cryptographic Support for z/OS 3.1, FMID HCR77E0)
document.not_consulted: A z/OS 3.2 edition exists (SSLTBW_3.2.0); it was not read.

conventions.positions: 1-based positions in the COBOL CALL ... USING list; return_code is 1.
conventions.keywords: Keywords are 8-byte fields, left-justified and blank-padded, unless noted. rule_array is contiguous 8-byte slots; rule_array_count says how many are filled.
conventions.weak_basis: 'ibm' marks a weakness IBM itself states (key size in bits, compliance-mode exclusion, 'strongly discouraged'). 'judgement' marks the analyser's own classification of an algorithm IBM documents neutrally.

sources.title: Callable service syntax
sources.fact: COBOL form is CALL 'CSNBxxxx' USING return_code, reason_code, exit_data_length, exit_data, parameter_5 ... in the documented order; CSFxxxx names can be used in place of CSNBxxx.

sources.title: Callable services with ALET parameters
sources.fact: CSNBxxx1 entry points take extra ALET parameters for data-space data; 64-bit ALET forms are CSNExxx1.

sources.title: Resource names for CCA and ICSF entry points
sources.fact: Maps each CCA name (CSNB/CSNE) to ICSF names (CSF..., CSF...6 for 64-bit).

sources.title: COBOL
sources.fact: IBM's COBOL sample calls CSNBKGN with key_form 'OP', key_length 'SINGLE', key_type_1 'DATA', then CSNBENC/CSNBDEC with rule 'CUSP' and an ICV of LOW-VALUES.

sources.title: Impact of compliance mode on callable services
sources.fact: Under PCI-HSM 2016 compliance mode, single-length DES keys cannot be compliant-tagged; default DATA key tokens cannot be compliant-tagged; compliant-tagged keys cannot use the SHA-1 hash method (stated for RSA keys and certificates).

services.name: CSNBKGN
services.title: Key Generate (CSNBKGN and CSNEKGN)

key_form._field: 4-byte, left-justified, blank-padded (IBM's COBOL sample declares it PIC X(08)). First two characters describe key 1, last two key 2.
key_form.OP: One key wrapped under the master key, usable locally. Required form for AES keys.
key_form.IM: One key wrapped under an importer KEK, to be imported here later.
key_form.EX: One key wrapped under an exporter KEK, to be sent to another system.
key_form.OPOP: Two operational keys with the same clear value, normally different control vectors.
key_form.OPIM: Same clear value: one operational, one importable.
key_form.OPEX: Same clear value: one operational, one exportable.
key_form.IMEX: Same clear value: one importable, one exportable.

key_length.KEYLN8: Same as SINGLE: DES single-length 8-byte key.
key_length.SINGLE-R: DES 16-byte key whose two halves are identical, so it behaves as a single-length key. Needs the 'Key Generate - SINGLE-R' access control point.
key_length.DOUBLE: DES 16-byte key; the halves are not guaranteed to differ.
key_length.KEYLN16: With a DES key_type_1: double-length DES key like DOUBLE. With key_type_1 AESDATA or AESTOKEN: 128-bit AES key.
key_length.DOUBLE-O: DES 16-byte key with halves guaranteed to differ.
key_length.KEYLN24: With DES key type DATA only: triple-length key in a version 1 token with an all-zero control vector. With AESDATA/AESTOKEN: 192-bit AES key.
key_length.TRIPLE: DES 24-byte key; the three parts are not guaranteed to differ. For DATA, a version 0 token with a DATA control vector.
key_length.TRIPLE-O: DES 24-byte key with three distinct parts.

key_type_1.AESDATA: Generate an AES DATA key; generated_key_identifier_1 is ignored.
key_type_1.AESTOKEN: Generate an AES DATA key using an AES token supplied in generated_key_identifier_1; key_length sets the size.
key_type_1.TOKEN: Key type is taken from the control vector of the token in generated_key_identifier_1; for DATA, key_length still sets the length. Not resolvable from the CALL alone.
key_type_1._token_only_note: These types are requested by passing TOKEN with a skeleton token carrying the right control vector.

key_type_2._field: 8-byte, left-justified, blank-padded. Used only for key pairs and only for DES; ignored when one key is generated.

single_length_des.condition: key_type_1 is a DES type (anything except AESDATA/AESTOKEN). SINGLE-R gives a 16-byte token whose effective strength is single DES.

SINGLE.why: 56-bit single DES key; IBM's compliance appendix says single-length keys cannot be compliant-tagged.

SINGLE-R.why: IBM: the replicated halves make it effectively a single-length key.

DOUBLE.why: Two-key triple DES; IBM does not guarantee distinct halves (DOUBLE-O does).

KEYLN16.why: Two-key triple DES only when key_type_1 is a DES type; 128-bit AES with AESDATA/AESTOKEN is not weak.

services.notes: key_length alone does not decide the algorithm: KEYLN16 and KEYLN24 mean DES or AES depending on key_type_1 (AES only with AESDATA/AESTOKEN). A single-DES key generated here makes any later CSNBENC/CSNBDEC/CSNBSYE/CSNBSYD call with that key run single DES, because those services pick DES vs TDES from the key's length. With key_type TOKEN the type comes from a skeleton token at run time. IBM's own COBOL sample generates an OP SINGLE DATA key.
doc_quirks: The AES key-length table spells the keywords KEYLEN16/KEYLEN24/KEYLEN32; the key_length parameter table spells them KEYLN16/KEYLN24/KEYLN32.
The DES key-length table marks a 'default' length per key type although the key_length text says a value must be supplied.

services.name: CSNBKGN2
services.title: Key Generate2 (CSNBKGN2 and CSNEKGN2)

rule_array.HMAC: Algorithm (required group): generate an HMAC key.
rule_array.AES: Algorithm (required group): generate an AES key.
rule_array.OP: Key form (required group): one operational key.
rule_array.OPOP: Key form: pair with the same clear value.
rule_array.V0PYLDK1: Optional: old variable-length payload format for key 1 (AES CIPHER/EXPORTER/IMPORTER only).
rule_array.V1PYLDK1: Optional: fixed-length payload format for key 1.
rule_array.V0PYLDK2: Optional: old variable-length payload format for key 2.
rule_array.V1PYLDK2: Optional: fixed-length payload format for key 2.

keywords.clear_key_bit_length: Integer: 80 to 2048 bits for HMAC; 128, 192 or 256 for AES. Overrides the token's length when key_type is TOKEN.

key_type_1.TOKEN: Type taken from the associated data of the token in generated_key_identifier_1.

key_type_2.TOKEN: Type taken from the token in generated_key_identifier_2; ignored for a single key.

HMAC with small clear_key_bit_length.why: IBM allows HMAC keys down to 80 bits.

services.notes: Exists. Generates only AES and HMAC keys in variable-length tokens wrapped with AESKW; the only algorithm keywords are HMAC and AES, so it cannot produce a DES key of any length. A single DES key needs CSNBKGN.

services.name: CSNBENC
services.title: Encipher (CSNBENC or CSNBENC1 and CSNEENC or CSNEENC1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Positional: slot 1 processing rule; slot 2 ICV selection; slot 3 algorithm. If the ICV selection is omitted (defaults to INITIAL), the algorithm moves to slot 2.

processing_rule.CBC: Plain CBC (NIST SP 800-38A); text must be a multiple of 8 bytes; output same length.
processing_rule.CUSP: CBC compatible with IBM CUSP/PCF; any length, output same length; a trailing short block is XORed with the re-enciphered previous ciphertext block, and a text under 8 bytes is XORed with the enciphered ICV.
processing_rule.IPS: CBC compatible with IBM IPS record chaining; any length, output same length; short blocks are enciphered as in CUSP, but the OCV is built from the ciphertext rather than a re-enciphered block, so it can chain records.
processing_rule.X9.23: CBC with ANSI X9.23 padding of 1 to 8 bytes; always pads.
processing_rule.4700-PAD: CBC padded with the caller's pad_character plus a one-byte count; output is a multiple of 8.

icv_selection.CONTINUE: ICV comes from the OCV saved in chaining_vector by the previous call. Only with CBC, IPS, CUSP.

algorithm.TOKEN: Default. Use the algorithm marked in the DATA key token.
algorithm.DES: Use DES and ignore the token's marking.

services.algorithms: DES family only. key_identifier is a 64-byte DES token of type DATA, CIPHER or ENCIPHER, a label, or an X9.143 DES/TDES block.
services.single_vs_triple_des: Chosen by the length of the key in key_identifier: single-length gives single DES; double- or triple-length gives triple DES. No rule-array keyword selects it.
services.icv: 8-byte initialization_vector. Encipher XORs it into the first 8 bytes of plaintext before encryption; each ciphertext block is then XORed into the next plaintext block. The OCV (first 8 bytes of the 18-byte chaining_vector work area) can be passed as the next call's ICV, or picked up with CONTINUE, to chain records. The same ICV must be used to decipher.

single-length key in key_identifier.why: Runs single DES (56-bit); see CSNBKGN SINGLE/KEYLN8/SINGLE-R.

any call.why: Only DES/TDES are available; there is no AES path in this service.

constant or all-zero ICV.why: IBM notes that 8 zero bytes nullify the chaining effect on the first block; IBM's COBOL sample passes LOW-VALUES.

services.notes: No ECB keyword exists here; every rule is a CBC variant. Weakness is decided by the key (its length, set when it was generated) and by the ICV, not by a keyword. CUSP/IPS short blocks are enciphered stream-fashion from the previous block or the ICV, so with a fixed ICV a message under 8 bytes is XORed with a fixed keystream.
doc_quirks: The overview list names the rules 'ANSI X9.23' and 'IBM 4700'; the keywords are X9.23 and 4700-PAD.

services.name: CSNBDEC
services.title: Decipher (CSNBDEC or CSNBDEC1 and CSNEDEC or CSNEDEC1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Positional: slot 1 processing rule; slot 2 ICV selection; slot 3 algorithm. If the ICV selection is omitted (defaults to INITIAL), the algorithm moves to slot 2.

processing_rule.CBC: Plain CBC (NIST SP 800-38A); text must be a multiple of 8 bytes; output same length.
processing_rule.CUSP: CBC compatible with IBM CUSP/PCF; any length, output same length; a trailing short block is XORed with the re-enciphered previous ciphertext block, and a text under 8 bytes is XORed with the enciphered ICV.
processing_rule.IPS: CBC compatible with IBM IPS record chaining; any length, output same length; short blocks are enciphered as in CUSP, but the OCV is built from the ciphertext rather than a re-enciphered block, so it can chain records.
processing_rule.X9.23: CBC with ANSI X9.23 padding removed; ciphertext must be a multiple of 8.
processing_rule.4700-PAD: CBC with IBM 4700 padding removed; ciphertext must be a multiple of 8.

icv_selection.CONTINUE: ICV comes from the OCV saved in chaining_vector by the previous call. Only with CBC, IPS, CUSP.

algorithm.TOKEN: Default. Use the algorithm marked in the DATA key token.
algorithm.DES: Use DES and ignore the token's marking.

services.algorithms: DES family only. key_identifier is a 64-byte DES token of type DATA, CIPHER or DECIPHER, a label, or an X9.143 DES/TDES block.
services.single_vs_triple_des: Chosen by the length of the key in key_identifier: single-length gives single DES; double- or triple-length gives triple DES.
services.icv: 8-byte initialization_vector. Each ciphertext block is deciphered and XORed with the ICV (first block) or the previous ciphertext block. Must equal the ICV used to encipher.
services.notes: Unlike CSNBENC there is no pad_character, so chaining_vector is position 11 and clear_text position 12. Same rule-array keywords and positional layout as CSNBENC; no ECB.

services.name: CSNBSYE
services.title: Symmetric Key Encipher (CSNBSYE or CSNBSYE1 and CSNESYE or CSNESYE1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Not positional: one keyword per group (algorithm required; processing rule, key rule, ICV selection optional).

rule_array.AES: Algorithm (required): AES, 16-byte block, 16/24/32-byte key. Not with CUSP, IPS or X9.23.
rule_array.DES: Algorithm (required): DES; single DES or TDES chosen by key length (8, 16 or 24 bytes). Not with CTR or GCM.
rule_array.CBC: Mode (default): CBC; text a multiple of the block size.
rule_array.CBC-CS: CBC with ciphertext stealing (CBC-CS1); text at least one block.
rule_array.CFB: Cipher feedback with segment = block size.
rule_array.CFB-LCFB: Cipher feedback with caller-set segment size in key_parms (1 byte).
rule_array.CTR: Counter mode; key_parms gives how many low-order counter bytes increment. AES only.
rule_array.CUSP: CBC compatible with IBM CUSP/PCF; any length. DES only.
rule_array.ECB: Electronic codebook; no ICV; text a multiple of the block size.
rule_array.GCM: Galois/Counter mode; key_parms_length is the tag length, key_parms holds the tag, optional_data holds AAD. AES only.
rule_array.GCM-LG: GCM producing/checking legacy tags (pre-OA46558) for 256 MiB or larger inputs.
rule_array.IPS: CBC compatible with IBM IPS; any length. DES only.
rule_array.PKCS-PAD: CBC with PKCS padding; always pads.
rule_array.X9.23: CBC with ANSI X9.23 padding. DES only.
rule_array.KEY-CLR: Key rule (default): key_identifier holds the clear key value; key_identifier_length is its byte length.
rule_array.KEYIDENT: Key rule: key_identifier is an internal clear token or a CKDS label (clear or encrypted key); key_identifier_length must be 64.
rule_array.INITIAL: ICV selection (default): ICV from initialization_vector. Not with GCM.
rule_array.CONTINUE: ICV selection: ICV from the OCV in chain_data. Not with ECB, GCM, X9.23.
rule_array.FINAL: ICV selection: ICV from chain_data; last piece of chained data. CBC, CBC-CS, CFB, CFB-LCFB, CTR, OFB.
rule_array.ONLY: ICV selection: ICV from initialization_vector; whole message in one call. CBC, CBC-CS, CFB, CFB-LCFB, CTR, GCM, OFB.

services.algorithms: AES (128/192/256-bit) and DES (56-, 112- or 168-bit key, by key length). Clear keys, clear tokens, or CKDS labels.
services.icv: initialization_vector, length in initialization_vector_length (block size; NIST-recommended 12 bytes for GCM). Used by every mode except ECB, where it is ignored. The OCV is kept in chain_data (first 8 bytes for DES, first 16 for AES) and can feed the next call.

DES with an 8-byte key.why: Single DES with a 56-bit key; IBM lists 56-, 112- and 168-bit DES key sizes and picks single DES for an 8-byte key. With KEY-CLR a key_identifier_length of 8 shows it; with KEYIDENT the length is inside the token.

DES.why: Even 16/24-byte keys give TDES with an 8-byte block.

ECB.why: No chaining; identical blocks give identical ciphertext.

GCM with key_parms_length 4 or 8.why: IBM: tag lengths of 4 or 8 are strongly discouraged.

KEY-CLR.why: Not an algorithm weakness: the clear key value sits in program storage. It is the default when no key rule is given.

services.notes: The algorithm keyword is always present (AES or DES). DES plus an 8-byte key is single DES. ECB is a keyword here, unlike CSNBENC. Default mode when none is given is CBC.
doc_quirks: The introduction mentions 'ICV selection rules FIRST and MIDDLE', which are not in the keyword table (INITIAL, CONTINUE, FINAL, ONLY). Not verified as keywords.
The CSNBSYE1 format names position 7 'length'; the parameter description calls it key_identifier_length.

services.name: CSNBSYD
services.title: Symmetric Key Decipher (CSNBSYD or CSNBSYD1 and CSNESYD or CSNESYD1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Not positional: one keyword per group (algorithm required; processing rule, key rule, ICV selection optional).

rule_array.AES: Algorithm (required): AES, 16-byte block, 16/24/32-byte key. Not with CUSP, IPS or X9.23.
rule_array.DES: Algorithm (required): DES; single DES or TDES chosen by key length (8, 16 or 24 bytes). Not with CTR or GCM.
rule_array.CBC: Mode (default): CBC; text a multiple of the block size.
rule_array.CBC-CS: CBC with ciphertext stealing (CBC-CS1); text at least one block.
rule_array.CFB: Cipher feedback with segment = block size.
rule_array.CFB-LCFB: Cipher feedback with caller-set segment size in key_parms (1 byte).
rule_array.CTR: Counter mode; key_parms gives how many low-order counter bytes increment. AES only.
rule_array.CUSP: CBC compatible with IBM CUSP/PCF; any length. DES only.
rule_array.ECB: Electronic codebook; no ICV; text a multiple of the block size.
rule_array.GCM: Galois/Counter mode; key_parms_length is the tag length, key_parms holds the tag, optional_data holds AAD. AES only.
rule_array.GCM-LG: GCM producing/checking legacy tags (pre-OA46558) for 256 MiB or larger inputs.
rule_array.IPS: CBC compatible with IBM IPS; any length. DES only.
rule_array.PKCS-PAD: CBC with PKCS padding; always pads.
rule_array.X9.23: CBC with ANSI X9.23 padding. DES only.
rule_array.KEY-CLR: Key rule (default): key_identifier holds the clear key value; key_identifier_length is its byte length.
rule_array.KEYIDENT: Key rule: key_identifier is an internal clear token or a CKDS label (clear or encrypted key); key_identifier_length must be 64.
rule_array.INITIAL: ICV selection (default): ICV from initialization_vector. Not with GCM.
rule_array.CONTINUE: ICV selection: ICV from the OCV in chain_data. Not with ECB, GCM, X9.23.
rule_array.FINAL: ICV selection: ICV from chain_data; last piece of chained data. CBC, CBC-CS, CFB, CFB-LCFB, CTR, OFB.
rule_array.ONLY: ICV selection: ICV from initialization_vector; whole message in one call. CBC, CBC-CS, CFB, CFB-LCFB, CTR, GCM, OFB.

services.icv: initialization_vector must equal the one used to encipher; ignored for ECB.

DES with an 8-byte key.why: Single DES with a 56-bit key; IBM lists 56-, 112- and 168-bit DES key sizes and picks single DES for an 8-byte key. With KEY-CLR a key_identifier_length of 8 shows it; with KEYIDENT the length is inside the token.

DES.why: Even 16/24-byte keys give TDES with an 8-byte block.

ECB.why: No chaining; identical blocks give identical ciphertext.

GCM with key_parms_length 4 or 8.why: IBM: tag lengths of 4 or 8 are strongly discouraged.

KEY-CLR.why: Not an algorithm weakness: the clear key value sits in program storage. It is the default when no key rule is given.

services.notes: Same keywords as CSNBSYE. Positions 16 to 19 are swapped relative to CSNBSYE: cipher_text_length, cipher_text, clear_text_length, clear_text.
doc_quirks: The introduction mentions ICV selection rules FIRST and MIDDLE, which are not in the keyword table.

services.name: CSNBSAE
services.title: Symmetric Algorithm Encipher (CSNBSAE or CSNBSAE1 and CSNESAE or CSNESAE1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Not positional: one keyword per group.

rule_array.DES: Algorithm: DES, valid only with the AS2805 rules A28MACGN, A28MACVR, A28OWFEC, A28OWFCL.
rule_array.CBC: AES mode (default): CBC; multiple of 16 bytes.
rule_array.ECB: AES mode: electronic codebook; multiple of 16 bytes; no IV.
rule_array.GCM: AES mode: Galois/Counter; tag length in key_parms_length, tag in key_parms, AAD in optional_data.
rule_array.PKCS-PAD: AES mode: CBC with PKCS padding.
rule_array.X9.23PAD: AES mode: CBC with X9.23 padding.
rule_array.A28MACGN: DES rule: generate an AS2805.5.4 MAC with a double-length DES MAC key.
rule_array.A28MACVR: DES rule: verify an AS2805.5.4 MAC; needs a residue keyword.
rule_array.A28OWFCL: DES rule: AS2805.5.4 one-way function over clear chain_data with a double-length DES CIPHER key.
rule_array.A28OWFEC: DES rule: AS2805.5.4 one-way function over ECB-encrypted chain_data.
rule_array.A28RES: Residue (with A28MACVR): chain_data holds a residue.
rule_array.KEYIDENT: Key rule (required): key_identifier is a secure key token or CKDS label.
rule_array.INITIAL: ICV selection: IV from initialization_vector; default for CBC and PKCS-PAD; not with GCM.
rule_array.CONTINUE: ICV selection: IV from chain_data; CBC or PKCS-PAD only.
rule_array.ONLY: ICV selection: single request; required for GCM; default for the A28 rules.

services.algorithms: Data encryption is AES only. DES appears only for AS2805 MAC and one-way-function processing with double-length DES keys.
services.icv: initialization_vector holds the IV for CBC, GCM, PKCS-PAD and X9.23PAD; ignored for ECB and the A28 rules.

GCM with key_parms_length 4 or 8.why: IBM: tag lengths of 4 or 8 are strongly discouraged.

DES (A28*).why: Double-length DES keys for AS2805 MAC/OWF; not data encryption.

services.notes: Exists. Secure keys only (KEYIDENT is the only key rule). DES cannot be used to encipher data here.

services.name: CSNBSAD
services.title: Symmetric Algorithm Decipher (CSNBSAD or CSNBSAD1 and CSNESAD or CSNESAD1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Not positional: one keyword per group.

rule_array.GCM: Mode: Galois/Counter; tag verified before data is returned.
rule_array.KEYIDENT: Key rule (required): secure AES key token or CKDS label.
rule_array.INITIAL: ICV selection: default for CBC and PKCS-PAD; not with GCM.
rule_array.CONTINUE: ICV selection: IV from chain_data; CBC or PKCS-PAD only.

services.icv: initialization_vector must equal the one used to encrypt; ignored for ECB.
services.notes: Exists. Positions 16 to 19 are cipher_text_length, cipher_text, clear_text_length, clear_text.
doc_quirks: The CSNBSAD1 format names position 7 'key_length'; the CSNBSAD format and parameter description call it key_identifier_length.
The X9.23PAD description says the cleartext was padded 'according to the PKCS padding scheme'.

services.name: CSNBOWH
services.title: One-Way Hash Generate (CSNBOWH or CSNBOWH1 and CSNEOWH or CSNEOWH1)

keywords.rule_array_layout: Not positional: hash method (required) plus a chaining flag or, with BCRYPT, a salt flag.

rule_array.BCRYPT: bcrypt version 2b password hash (60-byte result); needs GENERATE or VERIFY; no chaining.
rule_array.MD5-LG: MD5 reproducing legacy values from before APAR OA33657, for checking archived hashes.
rule_array.RPMD-LG: RIPEMD-160 reproducing legacy values from before APAR OA33657.
rule_array.SHA1LG: SHA-1 reproducing legacy values (pre-OA43937) for texts of 256 MB or more.
rule_array.SHA224LG: SHA-224 legacy variant for very large texts.
rule_array.SHA256LG: SHA-256 legacy variant for very large texts.
rule_array.SHA384LG: SHA-384 legacy variant for very large texts.
rule_array.SHA512LG: SHA-512 legacy variant for very large texts.
rule_array.SHAKE128: SHAKE-128 extendable output; hash_length sets output size.
rule_array.FIRST: Chaining flag: first of a chained series.
rule_array.GENERATE: Salt flag (BCRYPT): hash with a random salt; cost in chaining_vector byte 1 (4 to 31).
rule_array.VERIFY: Salt flag (BCRYPT): verify the hash parameter.

SHA-1.why: IBM's compliance appendix excludes the SHA-1 hash method for compliant-tagged RSA keys and certificates; SHA-1 is also collision-broken (judgement).

services.notes: The hash method is always in the rule array; it never comes from a key. The -LG keywords exist to match hashes computed by older ICSF levels.

variants.csne_64bit: Every service above has an AMODE(64) entry point (CSNEKGN, CSNEKGN2, CSNEENC, CSNEDEC, CSNESYE, CSNESYD, CSNESAE, CSNESAD, CSNEOWH). Each topic prints one format and names the CSNE entry under it; no separate CSNE parameter list is printed, so the same list is implied (for SAE/SAD IBM states the B and E forms 'provide identical functions').
variants.alet_1: CSNBENC1, CSNBDEC1, CSNBSYE1, CSNBSYD1, CSNBSAE1, CSNBSAD1, CSNBOWH1 (and CSNExxx1) take the same list plus trailing ALET parameters for data in a data space. There is no CSNBKGN1 or CSNBKGN21.
variants.csf_aliases: IBM says CSFxxxx can be used in place of CSNBxxx. 31-bit ICSF names: CSFKGN, CSFKGN2, CSFENC, CSFENC1, CSFDEC, CSFDEC1, CSFSYE, CSFSYE1, CSFSYD, CSFSYD1, CSFSAE, CSFSAE1, CSFSAD, CSFSAD1, CSFOWH, CSFOWH1. 64-bit ICSF names add a trailing 6 (CSFKGN6, CSFENC16, ...).

unverified: That the CSNE (64-bit) parameter lists are identical: inferred from the single format per topic, not from a separately printed CSNE list.
Whether FIRST/MIDDLE are accepted as ICV-selection keywords by CSNBSYE/CSNBSYD: mentioned in the introduction only.
The z/OS 3.2 edition was not compared.

single-length-des-key.basis: IBM: SINGLE and KEYLN8 generate an 8-byte, 56-bit DES key, and SINGLE-R a 16-byte key with identical halves that behaves as single-length (Key Generate topic). NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2, Table 1, approves no single-key DES and disallows two-key TDEA for encryption.

weak-hash.basis: CWE-328 gives CVE-2005-4900 (SHA-1 is not collision-resistant) and CVE-2012-6707 (an MD5-based password hash) among its observed examples. NIST SP 800-131A Rev. 2 restricts SHA-1 for digital signature generation to where protocol guidance allows it.

fixed-initialization-vector.basis: CWE-1204. IBM (Encipher): CUSP and IPS encipher a short block from the ICV, so a fixed ICV is a fixed keystream for a message under 8 bytes, and in every CBC rule equal plaintexts give equal ciphertexts. ECB uses no vector, and CONTINUE takes it from the previous call's chaining vector.
